question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x)+3 & =9 \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x) & =6 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The logarithm is a natural logarithm, which means its base is $e.$ So, we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x) & =3 \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x)} & ={e}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x)}=1-5x.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-5x & ={e}^{3} \\ -5x & ={e}^{3}-1 \\ x & =\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{-5} \\ x & =\frac{1-{e}^{3}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
